mode: Stock ordinary InnoDB, native parameter and lexical profile, utf8mb4, empty sql_mode, default mandatory-primary-key setting.
scope: Native ALGORITHM and LOCK clauses of standalone ordinary CREATE INDEX, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX and resolved DROP INDEX. Include persistent, session-temporary and session-shadow ownership, ordinary and unique secondary removals, and an explicit physical PRIMARY removal. Leave dependent keys, non-InnoDB storage, generated keys and ALTER TABLE action lists tracked separately.

IndexChangePolicy.role: The checked DDL algorithm and requested lock level of an ordinary index operation.
IndexChangePolicy.structure: Native Algorithm and Lock enum values, closed as compatible at the owning CreateIndex or DropIndex boundary.
IndexChangePolicy.conditions: Temporary table changes and standalone physical PRIMARY removal cannot use INPLACE. On a persistent table, COPY and PRIMARY removal require a lock level other than NONE. A temporary table can accept COPY with NONE. No ordinary index creation or removal accepts INSTANT in this declared domain.
IndexChangePolicy.meaning: Carry the requested native physical implementation and allowed concurrency; omitted and explicit DEFAULT have the same effective request. Native realization depends on ownership mode, other transactions and the matching external table.
IndexChangePolicy.sql: Emit only the native nondefault immutable algorithm and lock tokens, each once. Render the same effective request in either written option order.

boundaries.persistentSecondary: DEFAULT and INPLACE admit every lock setting. COPY admits DEFAULT, SHARED and EXCLUSIVE.
boundaries.persistentPrimaryRemoval: DEFAULT and COPY admit DEFAULT, SHARED and EXCLUSIVE. INPLACE and NONE fail.
boundaries.temporary: DEFAULT and COPY admit all lock settings. INPLACE fails.
boundaries.instant: Reject before completing an index value. Legacy servers report an unknown algorithm, and modern servers reject unsupported INSTANT or INSTANT with a nondefault lock. Record the actual native diagnostic per point.
boundaries.keys: InnoDB accepts at most 64 declared keys on a table in this profile, counting an explicit PRIMARY among the 64. An internal hidden row identifier is not a declared key. Creation is valid from 63 already-declared indexes and requires a known spare position; a source with 64 cannot accept another. Source key count is an externally interpreted property of the owning declaration.

finite.order: Enumerate the policy pair independently of admissible constructor values. Require matched native admission on every release, either the exact typed refusal or the corresponding successful construction, plus all fixed ordinary key-count boundaries.

observations: Before and after catalog, typed rows, exact target, lifetime and retained keys, including uniqueness and the transaction marker.

The written request's precise effective algorithm and lock in analyzed results, direct results and rendered SQL. A default, explicit NONE and SHARED are distinct except for the stock physical result on temporary tables.
Compare typed native refusal for every disallowed option pair without weakening the output or allowed input and admission domains. Record the measured affected rows and diagnostic categories.
faults: Allow INPLACE on a temporary table.
Admit INSTANT as a type that can be rendered.
Do not count an explicit primary key toward the known limit.
Change the successful key order or retained effects.
trust: Native engine choice and lock behavior for the same emitted constraints, the declared owner key catalog, exact closed construction methods and externally controlled native and distribution evidence.
